items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I got my master’s degree from McCartney University. He was a good boss.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Yeah. It was a great education. I got my master’s degree from McCartney University. He was a good boss. I mean he’s still — we went to Japan and he got busted on the way in. He wasn’t that good a boss, in that respect. But as a creative boss, in terms of being in a creative situation, the first time I recorded a guitar solo with him we were doing a song called “To You.” And I was playing in the studio and Paul was in the control room with an Eventide harmonizer changing the pitch of every note I was…
over the years I really learned the value of. But there’s nothing like playing it in A and putting the capo on the second fret.

items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was in Wings from ’78 to ’81. And the picture next to that is Paul McCartney with a concertina sitting on the balcony of a castle, a twelfth century castle on the south coast of England when we were recording.

ctx.x: I was in Wings from ’78 to ’81. And the picture next to that is Paul McCartney with a concertina sitting on the balcony of a castle, a twelfth century castle on the south coast of England when we were recording. The one above that is Linda McCartney at a Hammond B3 organ, and you can’t really see clearly but on top of the organ there is a pack of Senior Service, Players Senior Service cigarettes, no filtertips, which is what Paul smoked at the time. There’s a cup of tea, a scotch and Coke, a bunch of boxes of…
Well I have a burning question here, do your grandchildren get to play with your guitars?
